newsitem.title: UK: LME keeping eye on copper and zinc - CEO.
newsitem.headline: LME keeping eye on copper and zinc - CEO.

text.p: The London Metal Exchange (LME) is keeping an eye on its copper and zinc markets, although, as always, it monitors all its contracts, LME Chief Executive David King said.
"We are taking an interest in copper and zinc, which are sensitive at the moment," he said.
In copper, the market is currently finely-balanced, while in zinc stocks have fallen considerably, King said.

Copper market attention in recent sessions has increasingly focused on July tightness, ahead of next week's "third Wednesday" pricing. On Friday, July/one day was at a backwardation of $13, July for one week was at $47, and July/threes at $122.

The tightness is concentrated from next Wednesday, the July date, to the end of the month. July/August was trading at $90 backwardation, but beyond there, premiums are softer at $20 for August/September.

Traders said the tightness has been well-signposted, but could nevertheless whip out next week when the key dates become prompt. Some said there had been talk that within the next two weeks the daily backwardation would be at the LME's permissible one percent of cash limit - around $25.
"Whoever has got it is not likely to let it go," one said.
The long side of the market is believed to encompasass investment interests or a major merchant. On the short side there is talk that far Eastern players are being caught, traders said.

In zinc, meanwhile, there is no immediate tightness, with cash/threes at $9 contango. However, September to threes months is at a $12 backwardation, which traders believe reflects long-running Chinese shorts battling influential European merchant interests.
Talk of big deliveries of Chinese metal into Singapore has yet to really transpire.
"We keep hearing that there will be a big lump put on, but it never happens," another trader said.
Meanwhile, LME zinc stocks have fallen considerably this year. Inventories fell by 1,950 tonnes this week to 419,600 tonnes, and have dropped over 81,000 tonnes, or 16 percent, this year so far.
Zinc prices have responded to this, rising last week to 6-3/4 year highs of $1,495.
